title: Three Councils Rome counts as universal on images: Nicaea II (787), Constantinople (869), and Trent
source_text: III. Porro tria sunt Concilia quae Ecclesia Romana Universalibus accenset, quae de imaginibus & earum cultu agunt. Primum & antiquissimum est Nicenum secundum, celebratum anno Christi 787. Imperantibus Constantino & Irene illius matre. Secundum est Concilium Constantinopolitanum celebratum anno Christi 869. Imperante Basilio. Tertium est Tridentinum saeculo decimo sexto per plures annos celebratum ut omnibus notum est.
pass_a_gloss: Further, there are three Councils which the Roman Church reckons among the Universal ones, which treat of images and their cult. The first and most ancient is the second Nicene, celebrated in the year of Christ 787, under the emperors Constantine and Irene his mother. The second is the Constantinopolitan Council celebrated in the year of Christ 869, under the emperor Basil. The third is the Tridentine, celebrated through several years in the sixteenth century, as is known to all.
pass_b_english: Rome owns three ‘universal’ Councils on images: Nicaea II (787), Constantinople (869), and Trent in the sixteenth century.

choices.why: Names the three Roman authorities for the locus.
